item.title: China, Brunei to co-host ADMM-Plus Peacekeeping Field Training Exercise
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 -- China and Brunei will co-host the ADMM-Plus Peacekeeping Field Training Exercise in Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei, from November 27 to December 12, said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press conference on Thursday. "The exercise, codenamed Aman Damai Shared Future 2026, will involve personnel from different ADMM-Plus countries," Chen said, adding that the drill would focus on such subjects as battlefield reconnaissance, security patrol, response to terrorist attacks, and medical rescue. The spokesperson said that this event will help enhance the interoperability and technical and tactical competence of participating forces in peacekeeping operations, deepen substantive cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework, and safeguard regional peace and stability.

item.title: Japan disrupts peace and tranquility in Asia-Pacific: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 -- "We require the Japanese side to stop fueling tensions over the South China Sea issue. Any attempt to challenge China's sovereign rights and interests and undermine regional peace and stability will not succeed," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a regular press conference on Thursday. According to reports, the National Institute for Defense Studies under Japan's Ministry of Defense recently released the so-called China Security Report 2027. The report explicitly recommends Japan to sustain its presence in the South China Sea, strengthen minilateral cooperation with its allies and partners, and oppose China's unilateral change to the status quo by force or coercion. Japan's Ambassador to the Philippines recently stated that Japan will provide the Philippines with coastal surveillance radars and surveillance UAVs through the Official Security Assistance program. In response to the reports, the spokesperson pointed out that under the disguise of academic research, Japan, in this report, whitewashes its moves to meddle in the South China Sea issue and stoke tensions across the Asia-Pacific, and smears China's legitimate law-enforcement operations. This is yet another testament to the Japanese authorities' ambition to build up its armed forces and break free from the "exclusively defense-oriented" principle. The international community should stay highly vigilant against this. He also stressed that Nanhai Zhudao is China's inherent territory. Japan is not a party to the South China Sea issue, and is therefore in no position to make irresponsible remarks on it. During WWII, Japan committed numerous crimes in China, including the illegal occupation of China's islands and reefs in the South China Sea, which inflicted untold sufferings on China and the Chinese people. "In recent years, using so-called external threats as an excuse, the Japanese side has incited security anxiety among neighboring countries, supplied weapons and equipment to regional states including the Philippines, formed exclusive military cliques, and sought to enhance its military presence in the South China Sea by provoking confrontation," said the spokesperson, adding that, "Such moves have harmed the shared interests of regional countries and disrupted peace and tranquility in the Asia-Pacific."

item.title: 2026 Western Pacific Naval Symposium HADR Workshop and Tabletop Exercise to Be Hosted in early December
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov.26 -- The PLA Navy will host the 2026 Western Pacific Naval Symposium (WPNS) Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Seminar and Tabletop Exercise in Nanjing in early December, said Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a regular press conference on Thursday. "Representatives from member and observer states are invited to attend," Chen said, adding that under the theme "Multi-navy HADR in the Aftermath of an Earthquake", the exercise will focus on command chain integration, information sharing and operational coordination. According to the spokesperson, seminars will be held on topics including rule compliance, command organization and operational patterns for HADR activities. "The event will further deepen substantive cooperation on HADR in the Western Pacific region and enhance interoperability in crisis prevention and response," the spokesperson stressed.

item.title: China-Vietnam "Cooperation-2026" joint counter-terrorism training wraps up
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 -- The China-Vietnam "Cooperation-2026" joint counter-terrorism training successfully concluded in Hanoi, Vietnam, in recent days. Against the backdrop of jointly addressing terrorist threats and themed on jointly combating terrorist crimes, the joint training incorporated elements such as individual combat skills training, tactical coordination training, and comprehensive counter-terrorism exercises. Both sides conducted joint live-force drills including explosive ordnance disposal (EOD), battlefield first-aid operations, and counter-terrorism strikes in mountainous terrain. (Video Editor: Liu Sen)

item.title: Xi, Pakistani president exchange congratulations over joint spaceflight mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari exchanged congratulations on Wednesday on the joint spaceflight mission carried out by astronauts from the two countries. In his message, Xi said the joint space exploration of astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries, as well as another important achievement in bilateral cooperation. Xi said China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to champion peaceful use of outer space and deepen space cooperation.

item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 spaceship to Tiangong space station with first foreign astronaut on board
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Minggang) JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship on Wednesday, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani payload specialist, to its orbiting Tiangong space station. The spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. The astronauts aboard the spaceship are mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first-ever foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. The Shenzhou-24 mission marks the first joint flight consisting of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program.
